faqs.question: How long should I know a girl before proposing to her?
faqs.answer: There is no defensible number. The largest measurement available, a meta-analysis of seven samples covering 1,897 Canadian and US adults, reports friendships running from 1 to 180 months before romance began, with a median of 12 — a spread that wide gives you conditions to check, not a date to wait for.

faqs.question: Is one month too soon to ask her to be my girlfriend?
faqs.answer: It is too soon if you have not been alone together more than once, if she has not started anything herself, and if personal information has only travelled from you to her. A month is plenty of time for all three to happen, and also plenty of time for none of them to.

faqs.question: Do I have to be friends with her first?
faqs.answer: You do not have to, but most people were. In that same 1,897-person meta-analysis a weighted 68.2% had been friends with their partner before the relationship started, and 47.4% of one 298-student sample named a friendship turning romantic as the best way to meet someone.

faqs.question: How do I know if she likes me back or is just being nice?
faqs.answer: Politeness, quick replies and warmth in a group are neutral — they are aimed at the setting, not at you. Look instead for whether she initiates as often as you do and whether she has told you something she would not tell the group.

faqs.question: What if we have only ever talked in a group?
faqs.answer: Then the first condition is not met yet, and the honest next step is a plan rather than a question. A group supplies both an audience and a script, so nothing that happens inside one tells you much about how she feels one-to-one.

faqs.question: Is it too late if we have been friends for two years?
faqs.answer: Two years is close to ordinary. Friends-first initiators in one 298-student study had been friends a mean of 21.90 months, and the range in that sample reached 180 months, so a long friendship is not a disqualification.

faqs.question: Should I propose on Propose Day, or does the date not matter?
faqs.answer: Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February, the second day of Valentine week. A date can give you a reason to speak, but it cannot substitute for the conditions — asking on a calendar day you were not ready for is still asking too early.

faqs.question: What do I do if she says she needs time?
faqs.answer: Take it literally and stop asking. Follow-up pressure turns a pause into a decision, and repeated unwanted contact is not romance; give her the space to come back to it or not.

faqs.question: Can I ask over chat, or does it have to be in person?
faqs.answer: Chat is fine and often kinder, because it lets her answer without an audience or an immediate reaction to manage. What matters is that the message is unambiguous — a hint she has to decode puts the work of noticing on her.

faqs.question: What if she says no and we are in the same class or team?
faqs.answer: Plan for that before you ask, not after. Write the sentence you would say the next day, keep the ask private, and accept the answer — a refusal is information, and the shared setting is easier to keep workable than to repair.

faqs.question: Should I send a gift or a page along with the ask?
faqs.answer: Keep it proportionate to the ask. A marriage-proposal scrapbook is two steps ahead of a girlfriend question; a single personalised page she opens alone on her phone does the job without making the answer feel staged.

faqs.question: Does it matter that she has never had a boyfriend?
faqs.answer: Not for your timing. In a survey of 510 unmarried urban Indian adults aged 18 to 25, the most common age band for a first romantic relationship was 17 to 21 at 48.4%, so a first relationship at that stage is unremarkable — it just means the conditions matter more, not less.

article.contentMarkdown:
# When to Propose a Girl to Be Your Girlfriend, and When Not To

There is no number of days, so the real answer to when to propose a girl to be a girlfriend is a set of conditions rather than a date: you have been alone together more than once, she starts things about as often as you do, and personal information has travelled both ways. Any page handing you "two months" is guessing, because the largest measurement of how romance actually begins found the friendship preceding it ran anywhere from 1 to 180 months across 1,897 people. From this side of it, the page someone builds for an ask like this sits among 5,148 personalised pages created since 2026-03-12 across 21 page types on SubhSandesh, platform-wide, of which 38.5% are password-protected before sharing (1,983 of 5,148).

Below: what has to be true first, what does not count as evidence however much it feels like it, why too early and too late fail differently, and which page is the wrong one to send.

## What "propose" is asking for here, and why timing is the hard part

In Indian usage, proposing usually means asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend. It is not the marriage question, and this page does not treat it as one.

That distinction decides everything about timing. Marriage timing gets negotiated inside a relationship that already exists, with both people in the room; this ask happens before there is a relationship at all, so advice written for couples does not transfer. In [Pooja and Bhatia's 2026 survey of 510 unmarried urban Indian adults aged 18 to 25](https://spaceandculture.in/index.php/spaceandculture/article/view/1667), the most common age band for a first romantic relationship was 17 to 21 years, at 48.4%.

Already together and wondering how to escalate? That is a different post: [how to propose to a new girlfriend](/blog/how-to-propose-to-a-new-girlfriend) handles the escalation ladder, and [proposing for the first time](/blog/how-to-propose-girlfriend-first-time) handles the nerves.

## Five things that should already be true before you ask

None of these is a countdown. Each is checkable today, and the ask is reasonable when all five hold — which for most people takes months, and for some takes a year.

### 1. You have spent time alone together, more than once

**What it is.** Contact away from the group, the class or the office floor, arranged on purpose, at least twice.

**Why it counts.** A shared setting produces contact whether or not anyone wants it. Deliberately leaving that setting together is the first thing here that cannot happen by accident.

**How to check.** Count occasions, not hours. Twice is the floor, because once can be explained away by circumstance.

**What it is not.** Walking out at the same time, or a group of six that thinned to two.

### 2. She starts things about as often as you do

**What it is.** A rough balance in who sends the first message, suggests the plan and picks the time.

**Why it counts.** Volitional and mutual recognition of a connection is one of the defining features of a tie that has moved past acquaintance, in [the "fringeship" framework published by Fingerman and colleagues in 2025](https://figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/More_than_an_acquaintance_less_than_a_friend_fringeships_in_everyday_life/29447174).

**How to check.** Scroll back thirty messages and count who opened each thread. A ratio near ten to one is an answer.

**What it is not.** Her replying warmly every time. A reply responds to your initiation; it is not one.

### 3. Personal information has travelled both ways

**What it is.** She has told you something she would not tell the group, you have done the same, and neither of you regretted it.

**Why it counts.** Disclosure does not build closeness alone. Among 656 Seoul and Gyeonggi high-school students studied by [Woo, Kwon and Yang in 2014](https://ksppa.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/14855/journal-28-3-111.pdf), responsiveness mediated the link between self-disclosure and intimacy offline.

**How to check.** Name one thing she told you that you could not have learned from anyone else.

**What it is not.** You having told her a great deal. One-directional disclosure is something you did, not something you share.

### 4. She already knows, roughly, that you are interested

**What it is.** The ask should confirm something, not introduce it.

**Why it counts.** In [Stinson, Cameron and Hoplock's study of 298 university students](https://zenodo.org/records/5136908), 70.3% of the friends-first group said neither person entered the friendship out of attraction. Interest arrived later, and had to become visible before it became a question.

**How to check.** If a mutual friend would be surprised, she will be too.

**What it is not.** Hinting. A hint she has to decode is a test, and it puts the work of noticing on her.

### 5. She can say no and still have you around

**What it is.** A version of the ask that leaves the friendship, class group or team intact if the answer is no.

**Why it counts.** The setting usually survives the answer. You will share that corridor again on Monday, and planning for it is the difference between an ask and an ambush.

**How to check.** Say aloud the sentence you would use the next day if she declines.

**What it is not.** A public ask, or anything that makes a refusal cost her something socially.

## What does not count as evidence, however much it feels like it

Politeness is not interest. It is the default setting of most people in a shared space, and it is aimed at the space rather than at you.

Fast replies are not interest either. Reply speed tracks phone habits and spare hours far better than feelings, and the same person answers her group chat just as quickly.

Warmth towards you inside a group is the weakest of the three, because a group supplies both an audience and a script. Fingerman and colleagues' description of a fringeship covers this case exactly: regular contact in a specific setting, real fondness, a balance of small talk and personal disclosure, and no obligation at all.

That is a good relationship. It is not evidence that she wants a different one.

None of the three is negative evidence either. They are neutral, and reading neutral as positive is how people end up asking a month too early.

## Too early and too late both fail, and they look different

**Too early** is an ask she has no information to answer. She has met you in one setting, the disclosure has run one way, and the question arrives as a surprise she must handle politely. The usual outcome is not a no — it is "let's see", which is what someone says when asked to decide without the inputs.

**Too late** is quieter and more common. Mutual recognition is there, disclosure has gone both ways for months, and neither person says anything, so the tie sets into a shape that is hard to move. Stinson and colleagues' 298 students had been friends a mean of 21.90 months before romance began, median 12 — but the standard deviation was 28.23, larger than the mean, which is a statistician's way of saying nobody's case was typical.

Waiting and rushing are both expensive, and not symmetrically. Rushing buys one awkward week. Waiting past the point where the conditions are met can remove the option entirely.

## What the published numbers do and do not say about a wait

Here is every timing figure this page could find, beside what it was measured on and whether it yields a date.

| Claim about timing | Measured figure | Population measured | Gives you a date? |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Wait two months before asking" | none published | none named | No — no study attached |
| Romance usually starts inside a friendship | 68.2% weighted mean, N = 1,897 | Canadian and US students and crowdsourced adults, 2021 | No — same paper's range is 1–180 months |
| How long that friendship ran first | mean 21.90 months, median 12 | 210 friends-first initiators among 298 students | No — SD 28.23 exceeds the mean |
| Age of a first relationship, urban India | 48.4% at ages 17–21 | 510 unmarried urban Indian adults, 18–25 | No — an age band is not a wait |
| Time spent building a page before sending | median 2.2 hours, first save to last edit | sampled on the SubhSandesh apology dashboard, n = 1,375 | No — but it sizes your evening |

The takeaway is the last column. Four rows come from named samples, and not one converts into "ask on day 47" — so a page that gives you a number is describing its own confidence, not your situation.

## When a made page is the wrong thing to send

A [Will You Marry Me proposal scrapbook](/proposal) is badly oversized for this ask, and I would rather say so than sell it. It is built for a marriage proposal, ending in a YES button that grows every time they dodge it, and sending it to someone who has not yet agreed to be your girlfriend asks her to answer a question two steps ahead of the one you meant.

If the five conditions hold, the ask is small and the page should be too. [A personalised page for a girlfriend](/love-gf) says one thing, opens on a phone and ends; platform-wide, love-gf is the most-viewed template on SubhSandesh at 16,998 views, 29.9% of all page views. A private link she opens alone also gives her somewhere to think, which a scene with witnesses does not.

If the conditions do not hold, the honest next step is not a question. It is a plan — which is what [an invitation page that turns into a countdown](/date-invitation) is for: she answers a date, not a relationship, and you both get the alone-together occasion condition one asks for.

Platform-wide across 21 page types, 90.9% of started pages are published and shared (4,679 of 5,148), so building is not where people stall. Deciding is.

If the answer is no, that is information, not a problem to be solved. Accept it, step back, and leave the shared setting workable.

## Sources

- Stinson, Cameron & Hoplock, [The friends-to-lovers pathway to romance](https://zenodo.org/records/5136908), *Social Psychological and Personality Science* 13(4), online 12 July 2021.
- Pooja & Bhatia, [Types, patterns of romantic relationships and dating delays among urban Indian emerging adults](https://spaceandculture.in/index.php/spaceandculture/article/view/1667), *Space and Culture, India* 13(4), 27 March 2026.
- Fingerman and colleagues, [More than an acquaintance, less than a friend: fringeships in everyday life](https://figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/More_than_an_acquaintance_less_than_a_friend_fringeships_in_everyday_life/29447174), *Review of General Psychology*, 28 July 2025.
- Woo, Kwon & Yang, [Intimacy in online space](https://ksppa.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/14855/journal-28-3-111.pdf), *Korean Journal of Social and Personality Psychology* 28(3), 2014 — English abstract read; body is in Korean.

sources.stat: Study 3 meta-analysis of seven samples, N = 1,897 Canadian and US students and crowdsourced adults: median proportion .66 (95% CI [.59, .72]), weighted mean 68.2%, had been friends before becoming romantic partners. Study 4, 210 friends-first initiators among 298 students: friends a mean of 21.90 months (SD 28.23; Mdn 12; Mode 12; range 1 to 180 months); 70.3% said neither person entered the friendship out of attraction; 47.4% named a friendship turning romantic the best way to meet a partner, against 0.3% for an online dating service.

Survey of 510 unmarried urban Indian emerging adults aged 18-25 (221 men, 289 women) at universities across several Indian states: 48.4% began their first romantic relationship between ages 17 and 21, the highest-frequency band, rising above 60% among participants from nuclear families. One of the two most common patterns is the 'Romantically Friendly' relationship, in which friendship with the partner and with mutual friends is central.

Defines a 'fringeship' by four criteria: regular contact in specific settings; volitional and mutual recognition of the connection; freedom from the obligations of close ties; and a degree of shared affection, with a balance of small talk and personal disclosure. Theoretical review, no new sample.

656 high-school students in Seoul and Gyeonggi: responsiveness mediated the relation between self-disclosure and intimacy in offline space, and moderated it in online space. English abstract read; the body text is Korean and was not read.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine asked 'when should I ask her to be my girlfriend' currently has a choice between marriage-proposal timing pages and forum threads offering two months, five to eight dates or two to five years with no population attached. This page is the one that names the spread instead of a number — 1 to 180 months across 1,897 people, SD 28.23 on a mean of 21.90 — turns the question into five checkable conditions, and carries first-party platform figures no other page can publish. It will not outrank the incumbent lifestyle and jewellery domains on authority, and the two searches run were US-served, so the India SERP for this phrase is unmeasured; the realistic target is citation in an answer rather than a top-three blue link, and that takes months.

structuralLimitations: No proposal-specific first-party data exists: the proposalpages probe is still refused by this machine's production-read policy. Every figure in the body is labelled platform-wide across 21 page types, or sampled on the named template, in prose.
The pricing block in content/facts.md is empty for a fourth batch, so the post states and implies nothing about price, tiers or what anything includes.

Phase 1 is inherited and partial. Two of the four permitted WebSearch calls were used and both were served from the US; no top-5 page was fetched in full, so the post describes no competitor page's contents and asserts nothing about what rivals do or do not cover. None of this batch's keywords appears among the 11 India-served SERPs measured on 2026-09-16.

The Stinson, Cameron & Hoplock paper was read from the author-deposited CC BY-NC copy on Zenodo because journals.sagepub.com returns HTTP 403 to every client tried; the published version of record was not opened.
Woo, Kwon & Yang is a Korean-language paper. Only the English abstract was read, and the post claims nothing beyond what that abstract states.
Fingerman and colleagues is a theoretical review with no new sample; it is cited for its construct and its four defining criteria, never for a statistic.

Two sibling cross-links (/blog/how-to-propose-to-a-new-girlfriend, /blog/how-to-propose-girlfriend-first-time) are blog slugs rather than TEMPLATE_LINKS entries. Waves 1-3 are merged to main but not yet published to Strapi, so both resolve only once those posts go live.
No number of days is printed as a rule anywhere in the post. Every numeric figure carries the population it was measured on.
